environment.description: Celery worker on RHEL 9 with custom SELinux policy module 'celery_worker_t' compiled from Type Enforcement rules. The policy confines the celery process to domain celery_worker_t via automatic transition from systemd (init_t -> celery_worker_t). File context rules restrict write access: allow celery_worker_t celery_data_t:file { read write create unlink }; allow celery_worker_t celery_log_t:file { append }; with celery_data_t applied only to /var/lib/worker/configs/** and celery_log_t to /var/log/worker/**. No allow rule exists for celery_worker_t to write to user_home_t, ssh_home_t, sshd_key_t, etc_t, or any other file context. Policy compiled with semodule and loaded in enforcing mode (setenforce 1, SELINUX=enforcing in /etc/selinux/config). Additionally, the PostgreSQL SELinux module restricts the DB socket access but the UPDATE privilege on all columns remains.

type_enforcement_rules: allow celery_worker_t celery_data_t:file { read write create unlink open getattr };
allow celery_worker_t celery_log_t:file { open append getattr };
